claimWitness.text: `herdr pane run` types text into the pane's shell for the shell to re-parse (confirmed via `herdr api schema --json`: no `pane.run` wire request type exists, it is sugar over `pane.send_text`) — a long, complex `bwrap [flags] -- <cli> [args]` command typed directly is at risk of shell re-tokenization corruption. The fix: write the Confinement Authority's prepared invocation to a launcher script under the Run's own protected directory (never worker-writable), then `pane run <paneId> bash <scriptPath>` — a short, unambiguous typed command with nothing for the shell to mis-tokenize. Once launched, the process is a normal foreground child of the pane's own pty (verified live: output streams incrementally, stdin round-trips correctly — nothing is "swallowed" by the intermediate script). The launched process is then registered into Herdr's own `agent list`/`agent get` tracking via `pane report-agent`/`report-agent-session` (existing client methods from the original P02H cell, previously unused), so it stays promptable (`agent prompt`) and observable exactly like a normal Herdr-launched agent — Herdr's own readiness gate independently cross-checks the pane's real foreground-process identity against the claimed agent kind, it does not blindly trust the registration.

entries.consumerStatement:
**`OperationRequest`** = `{ operation: OperationId, contract: ContractRef, input: Box<dyn Any + Send> }` — typed per contract; a built-in downcasts `input` directly, never through a decode step.

**No serialization for built-in providers** — the semantic contract is schema + version (`ContractRef`), but in-process representation is typed Rust through `OperationProvider`. `EncodedMessage` (contract id, version, content type, bytes) exists only at the external-process/WASM boundary ([External Provider Protocol](./external-provider-protocol.md)), never as a kernel type. Raw `OsString` argv is never a semantic `OperationRequest` — it stays inside the CLI adapter's transitional lane.

**`ProviderOutcome`** — not a nested `fgos.v1` envelope or HTTP response; the presenter owns public projection; diagnostics travel through the trace/evidence sink, never silently on compatibility stdout/stderr. Human-in-the-loop rule: §8.

entries.consumerStatement:
R1 is three crates: `fgos`, `fgos-host-runtime`, `fgos-distribution`. The legacy exec lane is a module inside `apps/fgos`, not a crate, because it is CLI-adapter-local (§4). `component-protocol` waits for R2 (only an external-process adapter needs `EncodedMessage`). Extract further crates only when pressure is real. Neither app owns provider selection; neither host use case imports another; every host feeds the shared authority/router/contracts layer, and provider adapters depend on component protocols, not host presentation. A component is not created merely because one proof verb is convenient (`gate-bypass` stays under its settled authority, not a manufactured `gate-policy` component).

Distribution selects and activates the trusted runtime (`fgctl`: acquire/stage/verify/activate/upgrade/rollback); host invocation routes inside the activated runtime. Packaging-distribution owns the onboarding command vocabulary: local `fgos init` adopts a workspace under the active identity on first use, `fgos doctor --fix` performs every later registered repair, and the target architecture has no separate `setup` verb. See [Runtime Identity And Activation](../packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md).

## 10. Release Boundaries

entries.consumerStatement:
| R1 — distributable Rust CLI host | Invocation kernel; `const` `OperationCatalog` / `RegistrySnapshot` assembled once at the composition root; two-stage authority; transitional CLI lane in the CLI adapter; native `distribution.build.show`; `fgctl`-driven install/activate/rollback proof. | External ecosystem discovery, WASM, chat, production gateway migration, a `setup` verb. |
| R2 — external process preview | Process protocol, supervision, fixture conformance, static manifest validation; one-shot CLI loads the derived cache by fingerprint, rebuilds only on mismatch; explicit test/dev roots. | Core replacement, signatures/marketplace, WASM. |
| R3 — production remote peer | Remote projector/presenter, native route adoption, per-operation Node semantic bridge only where needed; remote peer is the **project-local gateway** (current herdr, same release) composing the host-runtime crate in-process. | Parsing CLI envelopes as internal API; a future **shared multi-project gateway**, which never links a project runtime in-process and instead reaches it through the out-of-process Project Runtime Adapter ([Future Constraints](../packaging-distribution/future-constraints.md) §2) — itself a `remote-host-use-case` adapter inside the project runtime. |

Chat is a valid future peer but does not gate R1/R2 until a real chat adapter and its admission/interruption/presentation contracts exist. | File location | `bin/fgos.mjs` at the repo root | unchanged |

**The Node program is not relocated and not renamed in the source tree** (decided 2026-09-10). `bin/fgos.mjs` computes its package root from its own file location and imports `../src/...` relatively, so moving the entry alone breaks it, and moving the whole Node package would decide the Node-side repo layout that [Repo Layout Vision](../component-boundary/repo-layout-vision.md) §7 deliberately defers (and would mislabel `src/state`, `src/runner` — which `fgos-runner` keeps using — as "legacy"). The payload is therefore the current npm package exactly as `package.json` `files` defines it, staged whole by the release builder under the manifest's `components.legacyNode.root` (`libexec/legacy-node/` in a staged release) with the same relative layout as the source tree — zero import changes, `bin/fgos.mjs` and `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` both inside it. The identity is renamed (`legacy-node`), the file is not; a filesystem rename happens only when the payload is deleted.

The public `fgos` executable is the platform Rust host. It resolves the legacy payload as `join(activeReleasePath, components.legacyNode.root, components.legacyNode.entry)` read from the activation binding's manifest — never from `PATH`, never from the caller's cwd, never as an alternate package-manager `bin` entry, and never hardcoded. A `dev:<rev>` source activation declares `root: "."`, `entry: "bin/fgos.mjs"`, `entries.fgos: "target/release/fgos"`; a staged release declares `root: "libexec/legacy-node"`, `entries.fgos: "bin/fgos"`. One mechanism serves dogfood and production ([Runtime Identity And Activation](../packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md) §5).

`components.legacyNode` names a payload **root** plus an **entry** inside it, not a single file (proposed 2026-09-10 by the host-invocation stream, see [Legacy CLI Transition](../host-invocation-routing/legacy-cli-transition.md) §2): the legacy payload is the whole Node package as `package.json` `files` defines it, staged with its source-relative layout intact so `bin/fgos.mjs` needs no import changes, and `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` lives in the same root. The Rust host resolves `join(activeReleasePath, root, entry)` and nothing else. A `dev:<rev>` source activation declares `root: "."`, `entry: "bin/fgos.mjs"`, `entries.fgos: "target/release/fgos"` — the same fields serve dogfood and a staged release.

claimWitness.text: This track delivers the **code-panel multi-cell facade**, making `fgos-code-panel` the single unified entry point for all coding work requiring review and red-team scrutiny:

1. **Direct single-cell requests:** preserve the existing `direct-single-cell` path with no plan bookkeeping ceremony (requests that merely cite or reference a plan/phase path in passing, cite a plan file as an edit target, or cite a plan path as background context while directing a run/resume verb at something else, stay direct-single-cell).

3. **Coding test-policy overlay:** attach the risk-aware 3-tier test policy (`focused`, `affected`, `full`) to coding cells so tests run efficiently and proofs are reused across identical Git trees and environments.

claimWitness.text: | | Fix round 1 (`b46200de`... superseded, see round 2) | Fixed H-1 (cli-spawn now consumes Authority's prepared invocation), H-2, H-5 (capability defaults downgraded to `unconfined` with a named-gap comment, unblocking the group-thinking route), H-6 (fixture + real-loader-validated test replacing the tautology), red-team's unconfined-with-policy finding. H-3 (F-c fallback) was reported fixed but the reviewer's own recheck (op_055) found the production call sites still passed the SAME capability as both `capability` and `fallbackFrom`/`anchorCapability` — a no-op fallback, not a real fix. **Mid-round infrastructure incident**: the Lead independently discovered the LIVE global `~/.fgos/config.json` (outside this repo, unrelated to this diff) had `advise`/`code:review`/`code:debug` shipped with `required`+`host-write-denied` and no resolvable backend, breaking those capabilities on this machine right now — fixed immediately and out-of-band (edited to `unconfined`, verified live via `node src/runner/dispatch.mjs decide --for code:review`), independent of this cell's own code fix. |

| | Fix round 2 (`f47f5b8a`, "fix: preserve confinement fallback anchors") | Fixed the REAL H-3: `resolveCapabilityIdentity` (resolve.mjs) collects multiple candidate capability names internally but previously returned only one, discarding the original anchor no caller could then forward — now exposes both the resolved identity and the anchor it fell back from, and the 3 `cli.mjs` call sites forward the real anchor. Also fixed N-1 (`establishConfinement` no longer reports `confined:true` from `ownWorktree` alone — only a control that actually provisions something, `privateHome`/`isolatedSession`, earns that claim) and partially fixed N-2 (corrected the CHANGELOG's R7 bullet's `host-write-denied`/migrated-live-config claims, but the recheck below found the SAME bullet still overclaims a different way). Reviewer-recheck (op_058) confirmed H-3/N-1 genuinely closed, live-verified against the production path — and surfaced 3 NEW findings never previously reported: **M-1** the just-corrected CHANGELOG bullet still claims all 7 canonical capabilities got an explicit `unconfined` declaration; only 3 do, the other 4 carry no confinement key at all (an omission, not a declaration). **M-2** 2 of the "2 known pre-existing, unrelated" test failures in `dispatch-production-call-sites.test.mjs` — waved off across 3 separate prior review rounds (op_052/op_055/op_057) as unrelated flakes — are in fact caused by `loadRunnerConfigFromDir`'s `mergeWithGlobalConfig` (config.mjs:255-272) leaking the *operator's own live global `~/.fgos/config.json`* into the test fixture, turning an intentionally-omitted policy into an explicit `unconfined` opt-out; proven by isolating `HOME` to an empty directory and getting 16/16 green on the same file. This directly false-positived 3 consecutive review rounds and is a real, environment-dependent bug, not noise. **M-3** the SAME no-overclaim class as N-1/H-2, one layer deeper and now reachable in production: `buildConfinementRequest`'s anchor-inheritance (request.mjs:141-144) copies an anchor's confinement wholesale even when the anchor's own mode is `unconfined` with no `omitted` flag, so a capability that declared nothing inherits a durable "explicit opt-out" attestation it never made — reachable for real now that the operator's live config declares all 7 canonical capabilities `unconfined`. |

| | Fix round 3, attempt 1 (`--p04-fix3`) | **Lead process error, not an agent failure**: dispatched with `--cwd` pointed at the wrong worktree (`confinement-authority-implementation-track`, HEAD `a46d7c36`) instead of the actual P04 cell worktree (`confinement-authority-implementation-p04`, HEAD `f47f5b8a`). Fixer (op_059) correctly self-detected the mismatch via `git rev-parse`/`git worktree list` and reported `blocked` rather than attempting work against the wrong branch — the SAME diligence pattern this whole track's fix-round briefs require of every dispatch. Reviewer-recheck (op_060) also ran against the same wrong cwd and correctly reported the same mismatch. Both scored `failed` by the coordination engine. No code was ever at risk; the session (`confinement-authority-implementation--p04-fix3`) was abandoned unclosed rather than reused, per the known poisoned-authorization-slot rule (re-authorizing the same actor/operation/node triple under a new id in the same `coordinationId` does not take effect once an earlier attempt is recorded). |

| | Fix round 3, attempt 2 (`--p04-fix3b`) | `--cwd` corrected to the real P04 worktree. Fixer (op_061) then hit the coordination engine's own 35-minute dispatch ceiling with **zero output**: `exit.json` shows `exitCode 124`/`SIGTERM`/`timedOut:true`, and `result.json`'s own evidence shows `gitBefore == gitAfter` and `changedFiles: []` — the codex-herdr executor made no visible progress on the combined M-2+M-3 scope within budget, not a rejected/wrong-target task. Reviewer-recheck (op_062) correctly detected there was nothing to review (HEAD unmoved, worktree clean) and used the remaining time productively: independently re-verified M-1/M-2/M-3 are still live via its own reproduction (not relayed), and additionally **corrected op_058's own test-failure count** (V-1: a third failure op_058 had reported, `assignment-dispatch.test.mjs:203`, did not reproduce — confirming it as a load-dependent flake, leaving 2 stable failures, not 3) and recommended splitting M-2 into its two independent halves (isolating the fixture from the global config vs. the fact that naive `HOME` isolation alone breaks 3 other confinement tests because the bwrap backend registry also reads `HOME`). |

Reviewer-recheck (op_005) reported `failed` with a new [blocker]: it claimed `settleReceiptRunFromOutcome`'s moved assignment-path lookup resolves to `.../runs/assignment.json` instead of the real `.../assignments/<id>/assignment.json`. **Independently verified wrong**: `path.join(path.dirname(runDir), '..', 'assignment.json')` for `runDir='.fgos/assignments/<id>/runs/01'` computes to `.fgos/assignments/<id>/assignment.json` (checked with a literal `node -e` call) — the correct location, identical to the pre-existing pattern this snippet was moved from. Red-team-recheck (op_006) independently live-attacked the same path with the real on-disk layout and got `failed`/`failed` as required — corroborating the Lead's own check. Reviewer's specific bug claim was rejected; its real residual ask (no *persisted* regression test for the recovery-settlement and cross-pass paths, only for `executeAssignment`) was accepted. |

| `--i01b` | Fix round 2 (revise + recheck only, fresh session id) | Fixer (op_007) `done`/`verified`, test-only commit `04fd9b84` (53 lines across `test/runner/cli-spawn-reconciliation.test.mjs` and `test/runner/operation-choice.test.mjs`, zero production files touched — confirmed by `git show --stat`). Reviewer-recheck (op_008) `done`, verdict PASS, confirmed both new tests call the real production functions (`reconcileCliSpawnRun`, `chooseStageOperation`), not a reimplementation. Red-team-recheck (op_009) `done` but self-reported "FAIL (high)" on the cross-pass test, claiming it doesn't pass at HEAD. **Independently verified wrong**: ran `node --test test/runner/operation-choice.test.mjs` (full file, twice) and the isolated test by `--test-name-pattern` — 148/148 and 1/1 pass, deterministically, both times, matching Reviewer's own independent run. Red-team's own revert methodology only reverse-applied 3 individual production files inside a scratch worktree rather than a clean prior commit, which plausibly left an inconsistent intermediate state — not evidence the committed test is broken. Rejected per "Verified Decisions" (empirical, reproducible, repeated check beats an unreproduced audit claim). Red-team's one corroborated point — the recovery-settlement test is genuinely non-tautological (passes now, fails when `e9210446`'s production diff is reverted) — is accepted as the real proof this round needed. |

**Structural finding for a future Lead (new, worth carrying into `fgos-plan-loop` SKILL.md):** a follow-up coordination session that only dispatches driver-authorized `revise-candidate`/`*-recheck` positions (skipping the required first pass) can never auto-close via `closeSessionByQuorum` — `quorum.completed` only credits a role for its REQUIRED graph-position completion (`produce-candidate`/`review-candidate`/`red-team-candidate`), not the optional recheck positions, even though the recheck assignments genuinely ran and reported `done`. This is harmless (the session just stays `active` forever) but means a Lead should not expect `close.json` to work for a fix-round-only follow-up session — record the outcome in the cell trace instead of chasing a close.

claimWitness.text: | `--i04` | Produce (op_031) + first review/red-team (op_032/033) | Doer `done`/`verified`, commit `370df7d9`. Reviewer and Red-Team both returned **Request changes** with 7 combined HIGH findings (5 reviewer, 2 red-team, 2 overlapping): assignment inspection ignored the admission ledger and dropped a terminal current run's RunResult; cwd inspection never implemented the cwd aggregate contract (canonical identity, dirt, guard conflicts); the static no-recovery proof only text-scanned one file instead of following the public use-case's import graph; the Host Routing Boundary had no implementation or proof; and several required selector-status fixtures (not-found, conflicting) were missing. Independently confirmed by the Lead reading `runtime-inspection.mjs` directly (the doer's candidate was a thin stub, not the accepted D02 design). |

| `--i04` fix round 1 (same session) | Fixer (op_034) `done`/`verified`, commit `badc2c72`: admission-ledger-derived current run, cwd aggregate identity/evidence/guard-conflict contract, ownership-gated recovery hints, import-graph-rooted static proof, host-routing façade (`invokeDispatchInspectOperation`), and the missing selector-status fixtures. Reviewer-recheck (op_035, dispatched in the same `--i04` session against a stale unconsumed authorization that had to be reissued once — a `grantedContextRefs` mechanics gap, not a content issue) and red-team-recheck (op_036) both found 5 new HIGH findings: the fixer's revision had **regressed** RunResult interpretation (raw `JSON.parse(result.json)` instead of `interpretRunResult`), cwd inspection asserted `resolved`/`correlated` despite missing evidence instead of `partial`, verification still did not exercise the changed cwd/host-routing contracts, an unadmitted Assignment Run still minted a recovery hint, and a malformed sibling `run.json` was silently discarded instead of surfacing as `partial`. All 5 independently confirmed by the Lead reading source (`result()`'s raw JSON.parse; `owner()`'s missing admission-ledger check). Quorum satisfied at this point (doer+reviewer+red-team+fixer all ran once); session auto-closed. |

| `--i04b` (fresh session; `--i04` already closed) fix round 2 | Fixer (op_037) `done`/`verified`, commit `63ce31a3`: restored `interpretRunResult` for every present result; cwd inspection now fails closed (`partial`) on missing/malformed lock/workspace/projection evidence; `owner()` now requires admission-ledger corroboration (`assignmentEvidence()`), closing the unadmitted-run hint leak; `allRuns()` now tags malformed materializations instead of discarding them; added a real `bin/fgos.mjs` CLI-level regression test. Reviewer-recheck (op_038) and red-team-recheck (op_039) found one new HIGH each: reviewer — Assignment-selector `byId` Map silently collapses two valid materializations sharing one admitted runId, still resolving with a hint; red-team — two composite bypasses (a Run selected directly via `--run` did not check its own Assignment for a malformed sibling; the `--cwd` aggregate did not require every bound Run, not only the hinted one, to be admission-complete), plus a repeated host-routing proof-gap concern. Both functional findings independently confirmed by the Lead reading source. |

claimWitness.text: - `src/runner/dispatch/recovery-planner.mjs` (new): pure `plan(snapshot, evidence, requestedIntent) -> RecoveryRecommendation`. No fs/adapter/network imports — consumes already-read facts. Deterministic modulo `actionKey`/`expiresAt`. `actionKey` is derived from `(snapshotHash, controlEpoch, action, expiresAt)` so a still-unconsumed key cannot be replayed against a different action or a re-declared expiry.

- `src/verbs/dispatch/recover.mjs` (new): `dispatch recover <runId>` — without `--action`, a read-only, ephemeral recommendation (no session event, no mutation). Applying requires all five of `--action`/`--expected-snapshot`/`--expected-control-epoch`/`--expected-expires-at`/`--action-key`; the write path re-derives current state under a short CAS critical section, fenced against the Run's real P01 `run-lock.mjs` control-epoch generation (never a shadow `run.json` field), with the settled-status recheck sequenced as the very last read immediately before the write.
- Never imports from `src/runner/coordination/` and never appends a coordination-session event — standalone Assignment-owned Run recovery stays outside session authority, per the contract.

claimWitness.text: The FIRST produce attempt (headless `claude`) wrote a complete, substantially correct implementation (~900 lines across all leased files) but was interrupted by the executing account's own Claude usage/session limit before it could run `git commit` — no code was lost (still sitting as uncommitted changes in the worktree), but the downstream reviewer and red-team each ran the full 35-minute wall-time ceiling with nothing new to review and timed out, leaving two orphaned herdr panes (closed). A fresh round was opened, switching the doer/fixer executor to `agy-cli` (Antigravity, headless `cli-spawn`, no persistent pane — chosen for lower memory footprint over `agy-herdr`'s live pane, per explicit user direction after this incident), instructed to verify/finish/commit the existing uncommitted work rather than restart. `agy-cli` succeeded — it has broader real tool access than the Bash-restricted headless `claude` executor, so it could run the actual test suite itself before committing (`a01b52a9`).

That round's independent reviewer found 1 MEDIUM (planner blind to already-recorded recovery commands, causing duplicate `recovery-command-recorded` events for the same Run) plus several LOW/INFO notes; its own overall dispatch result was separately flagged `failed` by the dispatch infrastructure's cross-worktree dirt check, but this was a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE — an unrelated, concurrently-running session on the same shared machine was independently editing docs files in the main checkout at the same wall-clock time, and the safety check cannot currently distinguish "this round's own agent leaked" from "unrelated concurrent activity on a shared machine." The reviewer's own report content was read and accepted on its merits after independently confirming (`git log`/`git status`) the flagged files were genuinely unrelated. Red-team independently found the same root-cause defect from a different angle (F-1: a `close` recommendation's eligibility reasoning didn't match the real `closeSessionByQuorum` quorum rules) plus a LOW residual (F-2: an unsalted `actionKey` can be re-minted with a new `expiresAt` — accepted as by-design, since every other CAS field is independently re-validated against real current state, mirroring P05's own already-accepted `actionKey`-is-a-CAS-binding-not-a-secrecy-boundary residual).

claimWitness.text: Prove validate-plan fails safe and close the 3 proven Cell 6.1 red-team exploits, tests first: (1) string-only evidenceRefs classifying `reported`; (2) cross-pass staleness defeated by mtime manipulation; (3) tampered stored results consumed cross-pass. Fix round 1 then closes the Cell 6.2 red-team exploits: forged result.json (F2d), schema-valid verdict flip (F2c), mixed dead evidence refs (F4b). Harness: /tmp/redteam-6-2/attack-6-2.mjs. Fix round 2 closes the reviewer-found stdoutLog evidence redirect (review NEW-HOLE (c)). Harnesses: /tmp/redteam-6-2/reattack-6-2-r1.mjs, /tmp/redteam-6-2/reattack-ra3-control.mjs. Fix round 3 closes the red-team P4a chain: pinned-dir report plant + unbound result.json fields (settle-bound report evidence + read-back re-derivation). Harness: /tmp/redteam-6-2/reattack-r2-scoping.mjs. Fix round 4 (final) closes the red-team S3 family + the reviewer-LOW re-derivation upgrade with one rule — monotonic re-derivation (the settle-time verdict is the floor). Harness: /tmp/redteam-6-2/reattack-r3-final.mjs.

claimWitness.text: Node transition needs two adapters with different contracts. Treating them as one provider would create the false impression that captured CLI output is a semantic result.

**`LegacyCliPassthroughProvider`** — CLI-only. Receives preserved `OsString` argv, inherited stdin, cwd/environment, and signal context; returns pre-rendered stdout/stderr bytes plus process exit/signal termination. It never returns `ProviderOutcome` and is never reachable from remote or chat hosts. This is the only adapter most legacy commands need: the CLI adapter looks up `CommandRouteDescriptor[selector]`, and for `route_kind == legacy-cli` execs the Node payload directly (argv preserved, signal forwarding) and writes one invocation record through the shared recorder — without ever building an `OperationRequest` or calling `InvocationService`/Router.

entries.consumerStatement:
| File location | `bin/fgos.mjs` at the repo root | unchanged |

**The Node program is not relocated and not renamed in the source tree** (decided 2026-09-10). `bin/fgos.mjs` computes its package root from its own file location and imports `../src/...` relatively, so moving the entry alone breaks it, and moving the whole Node package would decide the Node-side repo layout that [Repo Layout Vision](../../../architect/component-boundary/repo-layout-vision.md) §7 deliberately defers (and would mislabel `src/state`, `src/runner` — which `fgos-runner` keeps using — as "legacy"). The payload is therefore the current npm package exactly as `package.json` `files` defines it, staged whole by the release builder under the manifest's `components.legacyNode.root` (`libexec/legacy-node/` in a staged release) with the same relative layout as the source tree — zero import changes, `bin/fgos.mjs` and `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` both inside it. The identity is renamed (`legacy-node`), the file is not; a filesystem rename happens only when the payload is deleted.

The public `fgos` executable is the platform Rust host. **The Node program is not relocated and not renamed in the source tree** (decided 2026-09-10). `bin/fgos.mjs` computes its package root from its own file location and imports `../src/...` relatively, so moving the entry alone breaks it, and moving the whole Node package would decide the Node-side repo layout that [Repo Layout Vision](../../../architect/component-boundary/repo-layout-vision.md) §7 deliberately defers (and would mislabel `src/state`, `src/runner` — which `fgos-runner` keeps using — as "legacy"). The payload is therefore the current npm package exactly as `package.json` `files` defines it, staged whole by the release builder under the manifest's `components.legacyNode.root` (`libexec/legacy-node/` in a staged release) with the same relative layout as the source tree — zero import changes, `bin/fgos.mjs` and `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` both inside it. The identity is renamed (`legacy-node`), the file is not; a filesystem rename happens only when the payload is deleted.

The public `fgos` executable is the platform Rust host. It resolves the legacy payload as `join(activeReleasePath, components.legacyNode.root, components.legacyNode.entry)` read from the activation binding's manifest — never from `PATH`, never from the caller's cwd, never as an alternate package-manager `bin` entry, and never hardcoded. A `dev:<rev>` source activation declares `root: "."`, `entry: "bin/fgos.mjs"`, `entries.fgos: "target/release/fgos"`; a staged release declares `root: "libexec/legacy-node"`, `entries.fgos: "bin/fgos"`. One mechanism serves dogfood and production ([Runtime Identity And Activation](../../../architect/packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md) §5).

Added in candidate — checked resolver status (2026-10-13): the preceding activation-binding paragraph is retained selected design. `apps/fgos/src/legacy_exec.rs:69-154` selects the release root from explicit release/dev environment bindings or executable-relative manifest discovery, then verifies the manifest and confined entry. The target identity status in spec.md remains `accepted-not-implemented`; checked resolver behavior does not certify the entire target contract. The ownership rule remains never from PATH, never from caller cwd, never as an alternate package-manager bin entry, and never hardcoded.

claimWitness.text: The semantic component protocol is versioned independently from public host protocols — `fgos.component.v1`, distinct from CLI `fgos.v1` and any remote API version. It carries: operation identity and protocol/schema version range; request ID and optional parent/correlation ID; typed request, result, and error payloads; deadline, cancellation, progress, and events where supported; capability context granted by the host; provider identity and diagnostics needed for tracing.

claimWitness.text: The safe ecosystem default: core operation and command namespaces are reserved; plugins add vendor-scoped operations, e.g. `acme.deploy.release`; plugins may implement extension points explicitly published by a built-in component; `.fgos` writes, Git mutation, process execution, network, secrets, and host callbacks require explicit capability grants; unknown capability requests and ambiguous claims fail closed. The provider manifest is never an authority source — caller admission and selected-provider grant (kernel contract §7) apply identically here.
